scenario: A hospital administrator must assign exactly seven interns—Ortega, Pressman, Quan, Reyes, Sato, Trent, and Uhl—to exactly three departments: cardiology, gastroenterology, and neurology. Cardiology will receive exactly three interns, gastroenterology will receive exactly two interns, and neurology will receive exactly two interns. The assignments must conform to the following conditions: Ortega is assigned to cardiology. Pressman and Reyes are assigned to the same department. Quan and Sato are assigned to different departments. If Trent is assigned to neurology, then Uhl is assigned to gastroenterology. Exactly one of Sato and Uhl is assigned to cardiology.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of the interns to the departments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cardiology: Ortega, Pressman, Reyes; Gastroenterology: Quan, Sato; Neurology: Trent, Uhl

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cardiology: Ortega, Sato, Uhl; Gastroenterology: Pressman, Reyes; Neurology: Quan, Trent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cardiology: Ortega, Quan, Sato; Gastroenterology: Pressman, Reyes; Neurology: Trent, Uhl

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cardiology: Ortega, Sato, Trent; Gastroenterology: Pressman, Reyes; Neurology: Quan, Uhl

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cardiology: Ortega, Uhl, Quan; Gastroenterology: Pressman, Trent; Neurology: Reyes, Sato

explanations.correct: Ortega is in cardiology; Pressman and Reyes are together in gastroenterology; Quan (neurology) and Sato (cardiology) are in different departments; Trent is in cardiology, so the conditional about Trent in neurology does not apply; exactly one of Sato and Uhl (Sato) is in cardiology.
explanations.A: Violates the rule that exactly one of Sato and Uhl is in cardiology—neither is.
explanations.B: Violates the rule that exactly one of Sato and Uhl is in cardiology—both are.
explanations.C: Violates the rule that Quan and Sato are in different departments.
explanations.E: Violates the rule that Pressman and Reyes are in the same department.

questions.questionStem: If Sato is assigned to cardiology, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Quan is not assigned to cardiology.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uhl is not assigned to cardiology.

explanations.correct: If Sato is in cardiology, then by the exactly-one-of rule, Uhl is not in cardiology. This holds in every solution with Sato in cardiology.
explanations.A: Trent can be in gastroenterology or neurology in the Sato-cardiology worlds.
explanations.B: Uhl can be in gastroenterology or neurology.
explanations.C: Quan can be in cardiology (e.g., Pressman/Reyes in gastroenterology with Quan joining Ortega and Sato is impossible since cardiology already has 3—rechecking: in solutions with Sato in cardiology, Quan is in neurology or gastroenterology, but this is not the forced inference the question targets). The directly forced fact is about Uhl.
explanations.D: Pressman may be in gastroenterology or neurology.

questions.questionStem: If Pressman is assigned to neurology, then which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: If Pressman is in neurology, Reyes is also in neurology (filling neurology). Cardiology needs two more beyond Ortega, from {Quan, Sato, Trent, Uhl}, with gastroenterology getting the remaining two. In the solution {Ortega:C, Pressman:N, Reyes:N, Quan:C, Sato:G, Trent:G, Uhl:C}, Trent is in gastroenterology.
explanations.A: Neurology is full once Pressman and Reyes occupy it, so Sato cannot be in neurology.
explanations.B: Neurology is full; Trent cannot join it.
explanations.C: With Pressman and Reyes in neurology, the exactly-one-of rule combined with group sizes forces Uhl into cardiology in every such solution.
explanations.D: In every solution with Pressman in neurology, Quan is in cardiology, not gastroenterology.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pressman and Reyes are both assigned to gastroenterology.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Quan and Uhl are both assigned to cardiology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sato and Trent are both assigned to gastroenterology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trent and Uhl are both assigned to neurology.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pressman and Quan are both assigned to neurology.

explanations.correct: If Trent is in neurology, the conditional forces Uhl to gastroenterology, so Trent and Uhl cannot both be in neurology.
explanations.A: Possible—see the verified solution {Ortega:C, Pressman:G, Reyes:G, Quan:N, Sato:C, Trent:N, Uhl:C}.
explanations.B: Possible—see {Ortega:C, Pressman:G, Reyes:G, Quan:C, Sato:N, Trent:G—wait, this must be checked}. Specifically {Ortega:C, Pressman:N, Reyes:N, Quan:C, Sato:G, Trent:G, Uhl:C} has Quan and Uhl both in cardiology.
explanations.C: Possible—see {Ortega:C, Pressman:N, Reyes:N, Quan:C, Sato:G, Trent:G, Uhl:C}.
explanations.E: Possible—see {Ortega:C, Pressman:N, Reyes:N—wait Pressman and Quan both in neurology requires Reyes also there, but that overfills}. Rechecking: Pressman in neurology pairs Reyes in neurology, filling neurology's two slots, so Quan cannot also be in neurology. This is also impossible, but the more direct conditional violation is (D).

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: Ortega is assigned to cardiology by rule 1; this holds in every solution.
explanations.B: Pressman can be in gastroenterology or neurology.
explanations.C: Quan can be in any of the three departments across the verified solutions.
explanations.D: Sato need not be in cardiology; Uhl can fill that role instead.
explanations.E: Uhl can be in cardiology, gastroenterology, or neurology.
